featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Rizvi College, Bandra, as my TYBSc board exam center, and overall I had a very good experience there. The atmosphere of the college was pleasant, calm, and well-suited for exams, which helped reduce stress and made students feel comfortable.

The teachers were strict regarding exam discipline, but they were also polite, helpful, and managed everything properly. The staff was cooperative and maintained good organization throughout the process.

I also liked the college infrastructure. The campus looked well-maintained, clean, and had a positive environment. It gave a good impression overall.

The only small improvement I would suggest is in the washroom facilities, especially for the English toilet. It would be better if handwash and tissue paper were regularly available for students’ convenience.

Apart from that, everything was very good, and I genuinely liked the college.

I am currently in my final year of B.Com, and unfortunately my experience with this college has been very disappointing. From the first year itself, I have been facing issues with Mathematics, and my result is still not being cleared properly till date.
The college authorities had assured that internal points would be given to help students, but in reality, no such support was provided. Because of this mismanagement and lack of transparency, students suffer academically as well as mentally.
After paying full fees, students expect guidance and fair evaluation, but instead, careers are getting delayed and lives are being affected. This situation also creates embarrassment for students in front of their families, which is very stressful.
I hope the management takes responsibility and improves the system so that students do not face such problems in the future

featured_reviews.name: Riddhi Shetkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I spent five wonderful years at this college, and this is my honest review. When I took admission, I had never even seen the college building—I joined purely based on trust and feedback. Looking back today, I can confidently say it was the right decision.
Over these five years, I not only focused on my studies but also truly enjoyed my college life. While some students choose to bunk lectures, there are many dedicated teachers here who teach with full commitment and always support students whenever they face academic difficulties.

The college offers various activities to make student life engaging and enjoyable. I was a part of NSS, and my favorite teachers were Meenakshi Ma’am and Raj Paul Sir. During my degree years, the teaching staff felt more like friends than strict professors. We never skipped lectures, and even when we attended lectures of other divisions, the teachers were always welcoming and understanding.

A college should not be judged based on the behavior of a few students. My personal experience here has been extremely positive. If you choose to learn while enjoying the journey, this college and its teachers will never disappoint you.

Also, a special mention—the best samosas and Schezwan I’ve ever had were here! This place truly felt like home to me.

Forever grateful to this college.
— A proud ex-student

**Location:** Situated in the heart of Mumbai, the college benefits from being in a prime location with easy access to transportation, cultural attractions, and industry opportunities.

**Alumni Network:** Rizvi College boasts a strong alumni network which provides mentorship and networking opportunities for current students.

**Overall Impression:** Rizvi College of Arts, Science, and Commerce is highly regarded for its academic excellence, supportive environment, and extensive opportunities for personal and professional growth. It continues to be a preferred choice for students seeking quality education in Mumbai.

I have had strict teachers in school, but they were always polite and professional. Here, the main faculty and staff were openly rude. I had some pending documentation work (which shouldn’t have been required since I was already a student). I went two days later, was told it wouldn’t be done, and still showed up every day at the HOD’s office for two weeks between 12–5 PM. I apologized formally with a signed letter. I traveled 2 hours every day just to get this sorted, and the HOD literally slammed the door in my face everytime . I was just 18 years old.

Thankfully, I changed colleges within two weeks after that. It was a completely toxic environment.

Lectures were scheduled from 12–5 PM, but after traveling 2 hours to attend, we would often be informed that the lectures were cancelled. There was no way to give feedback because of the extremely rude and egoistic HOD. Even parents of first-year students noticed how arrogant and disrespectful the HOD was.

The staff was horrible — lazy, unhelpful, and irresponsible. Nothing was ever done on time. Getting just one signature for a basic document from the principal (who comes every day) took an entire month because of the staff and they still did not do it . When I approached the principal’s assistant, he told me I could meet her anytime she was free. I went and the principal signed it in five minutes. The problem was clearly the staff and hod's, not the principal.

When I went to get my leaving certificate signed, another HOD(Senior one) taunted me about restarting somewhere else. I simply said it was better to leave a toxic environment, and it truly was. The college I eventually graduated from was actually good, and I am so glad I escaped this place as soon as possible.

Let’s ignore the staff, but the main coordinators will say harsh words that will break your self-confidence.

When I had left the college and just came to complete last formalities the Senior hod exactly said, " Restarting again, it’s such a waste of time, waste of everything." Imagine this one reply coming from the main hod a complete toxic environment.
The HOD are not strict, they are rude, ruthless, merciless and we have to beg for everything.

Fortunately, most of my first year was during COVID, so I was saved from experiencing more of this chaos — except for the last two months, which were enough to show me how bad things were.

Please do not enroll in any course here, especially not management courses. They will make you suffer.

The only good thing about this college was the visiting faculty. They were excellent, understood our concerns, and genuinely tried to help — but they had no authority since it was a government college. I realized the truth the hard way, after going through two miserable months. Even the student crowd wasn’t much of an issue — 99% of the problems came from the HOD and staff.

Fortunately, I got a lot time after joining my new college and with their support did a lot of things and upskilled my experience and myself.

A tip for recently 12th grade pass, please if you do not get into any college, take a gap but do not enroll here, this college will leave you mentally disturbed. I have faced it. It took a full 4 months for me to recover.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Nayar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What should have been a review has become a eulogy, as I was just informed that Dr. Sampat is no more.

A great principal isn’t just a leader; they are a force. They shape minds, build character, and leave a mark so deep that even years later, their words echo in your heart.

Dr. Urmi Sampat was that kind of principal. She wasn’t just an educator,she was an institution.

I still remember my first day at H.J. College. She stood at the gate in a crisp cream saree, radiating authority yet warmth. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Namrata  , and I’m am going to be the topper this year,” I replied with pride. She just laughed and said, “Go and sit yourself inside.” That was Dr. Sampat, no fuss, no unnecessary praise, just straight to the point. But in that moment, she acknowledged me. And with her, an acknowledgment always meant something.

She had this aura about her,if she caught you in the corridor, you’d hold your breath. If you were exhaling, you wouldn’t dare inhale again until she passed. That was the kind of presence she had. But beneath that formidable exterior was someone who truly believed in her students.

I remember struggling in my psychology paper. She called me in and asked, “What the hell have you done?” I admitted, “I had a blackout.” She didn’t let me off easily. “I don’t believe in blackouts, but I believe in you,” she said. And that belief changed me. I promised her I wouldn’t let her down. And when I topped my methods, she awarded me the prestigious Miss H.J Title of the year. That moment shaped my future in ways I didn’t even realise at the time.

One of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received came from her:

Personally, I see a junior Dr. Urmi Sampat in Namrata.
That comparison still humbles me.

Everything she taught me stayed with me. From my first lesson at NPKT to my journey as a teacher at Arya Vidya Mandir Bandra, to moving to Dubai , her words have never left me. The discipline, the passion, the high standards,they are woven into the way I lead today.

I wish I had the chance to say goodbye. But in a way, someone like her never truly leaves. Somewhere, I know she’s making sure everyone arrives on time, does their job well, and carries themselves with the grace and dignity she expected of us all.

Dr. Sampat, you were the epitome of grace, excellence, and discipline. They don’t make them like you anymore. I treasured you, and I always will.
Yours truly,
Namrata Simon Nayar

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Faisal Asfiyan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this email with deep concern and disappointment regarding my recent experience at the Ali Yavar Jung National Institute of Speech and Hearing Disabilities (Divyangjan), Mumbai.
This visit was not a routine one. I had come hearing test with an infant who is currently suffering from MDR-TB, which is already an extremely sensitive and stressful medical condition for any family. We had traveled nearly 70 kilometers with the expectation that the process would be handled with a certain level of urgency, care, and professionalism—especially considering the health condition involved.
Despite arriving at around 11:00 AM, I had to wait at one of the counters for nearly 20 minutes without any staff present. Even after multiple requests for assistance, no one attended the counter. When a staff member finally arrived, the response was rude and dismissive, simply stating that they were “short-staffed.”
While I understand operational constraints, I believe basic responsiveness, empathy, and professionalism should not be compromised—especially in cases involving infants and serious medical conditions.
I had already made a request to prioritize the process considering the medical urgency. However, there was no visible effort to accommodate this. The entire process of tests and procedures was completed only by around 2:00 PM thanks to one of the head she helped me with this.
Following this, I was asked to wait further for the report, which was finally provided close to 4:00 PM. This delay is difficult to understand, especially when the report appeared to be a standard document.
What added further inconvenience was the lack of communication regarding document requirements. I was informed much later that a passport-size photograph of the child was required. This could have easily been mentioned on the appointment slip or communicated earlier during the long waiting period. Instead, I had to urgently arrange for a photograph, which caused an additional delay of approximately 45 minutes.
In a situation where we are already under immense emotional and physical stress due to the child’s medical condition, being subjected to such disorganized processes, long waiting times, and lack of sensitivity is extremely disheartening.
This is not just about delay—it is about the absence of empathy, coordination, and basic patient-centric approach.
I sincerely request you to take this matter seriously and look into the following:
Improve counter management and reduce unattended waiting time
